title: The Last Letter: Fault Line
statement: Mara made Lumen's seam germinate and then made its reflection take root; both of them trusted the horizon to stay level. I didn't. The page has slipped along a fault: the left half of the seam and the right half no longer meet, the right side has dropped, and the whole field tilts a few degrees as if the letter were read in a moving vehicle. Where the two halves fail to join, a short vertical bar of hot orange runs between them, the one colour the dusk never contained. The five seeds went with their halves. A last line that breaks is still a last line; it just has two ends now, and whoever comes next can pick either.
process: I kept the parent's two-tone field, the glowing stem-seam and the five seed marks, then split everything at the vertical centre with two clip paths, dropped and tilted the right half, and drew an orange connector across the gap. The guide circles were cut by the same fault so the break is visible in every layer, not just the line.
